pending.description: Redesigned step-01-working-memory-cleanup to use rename (mv) instead of copy+delete for archiving working memory entries to episodic. The old pattern failed on every scheduled run for 33 nights because the sandbox cannot unlink files (Operation not permitted) but can rename them. New pattern: mutate frontmatter in-place on the source file first (set status:archived, add type:working-archive, salience.score:0), then mv to memory/episodic/{fname} — one inode operation. Added working_stranded counter and skipped_already_archived skip rule to handle dead files left by the old pattern. Trivial-body delete fallback now also leaves the file in place with status:archived on failure rather than losing it. Rename hypothesis verified empirically in sandbox: mv exit code 0, source gone, destination present. rm on the destination confirmed still blocked (unlink still fails). Added systems/sandbox-credentials/SETUP.md runbook for GitHub PAT credential flow via git credential.helper store.

files.description: Move-on-write redesign. Frontmatter mutation before rename. skipped_already_archived rule for dead files. working_stranded counter. No copy+delete anywhere. Trivial delete fallback leaves file in place on failure.

pending.description: Rotation-proof GitHub PAT credential flow for Cowork sandbox git push. Root problem: the Cowork session ID (e.g., sleepy-blissful-meitner) rotates on sandbox rebuild, breaking any hardcoded absolute path in credential.helper. Solution: a committed shell script at systems/sandbox-credentials/git-credential-helper.sh resolves its own directory at runtime via $(dirname "$0"), then reads .git-credentials from that same directory. Git is configured with credential.helper = '!$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/systems/sandbox-credentials/git-credential-helper.sh' — the stored value contains no session ID. Empirically verified in sandbox: git credential fill returns correct username/password; stored config value confirmed session-ID-free. Script is committed and executable; credentials file lives at systems/sandbox-credentials/.git-credentials (600 perms, gitignored). One-time setup on David's Mac; no per-session steps required.

files.description: Updated runbook: rotation-proof credential design using committed shell script + git rev-parse path resolution. Replaces the original hardcoded-session-ID store approach. Covers PAT generation, 1Password storage, credential file placement, git config wiring, executable verification, end-to-end test, and 90-day rotation. Includes empirical test evidence from session sleepy-blissful-meitner.

New credential helper script. Reads credentials from .git-credentials in the same directory as the script. Handles get action only; store/erase are no-ops. Exits cleanly if credentials file is missing. Contains no token — path resolution only. Must be executable (chmod +x).

pending.description: IES Eval Harness — 4-Tier Assessment Framework. Full system instrumentation for workflows, skills, and agents with automated Tier 1 (mechanical success/fail), Tier 2 (structural assertions), Tier 3 (on-demand letter grading), and Tier 4 (controller feedback sampling) assessment. Includes 4 hook scripts wired into Claude Code lifecycle (SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PostToolUseFailure, SessionEnd), 6 assertion definition files covering all major workflows and the eval skills themselves, 3 new skills (rigby-eval-grade, rigby-eval-analyze, rigby-eval-dashboard), an HTML dashboard generator, eval schema, and integration into weekly-review, daily-review, and evolution-deployment workflows. Post-build adversarial review applied 15 fixes: Tier 2 assertion lookup (name over agent-type), Tier 1 no longer overwrites with hardcoded values, agent_id stored in stubs for reliable correlation, yaml import moved to top-level, tool_failure increments preserved through stop hook, failure_entry attached to records, all hooks use IES_ROOT env var, atomic writes with fcntl locking, trigger detection from state.yaml, log_error/log_info separated, weekly-review step-08 owns workflow close, daily-review and evolution-deployment assertion files added, self-assertion files for eval skills, benchmark snapshot comparison clarified as deferred, and weekly-review routing table corrected.

pending.description: Built SkillOpt-style optimization loop for IES skills. Implements the text-space skill optimization paradigm from arXiv:2605.23904 (Microsoft/SJTU, May 2026) adapted to IES architecture: uses the 4-tier eval harness as the scoring signal, IES composite score formula as the gate criterion, and a new rigby-skill-reflect skill as the reflection engine. Core components: (1) rigby-skill-reflect — trajectory-to-edits reflection skill that reads eval records + session transcripts, separates successes from failures, identifies procedural patterns, and proposes bounded add/delete/replace edits to SKILL.md files; (2) 8-step skill-optimize workflow — setup, baseline scoring, reflect, apply candidate, score candidate, gate, slow update, report; (3) score_eval.py — authoritative Python implementation of the composite scoring formula (mechanical×0.25 + assertion_rate×0.35 + grade_score×0.20 + feedback×0.10 + no_errors×0.10) with weight redistribution for null components; (4) manifest and Rigby agent updates. Key architectural decisions: simulated improvement assessment for gate (IES cannot re-run skills with candidate versions), SLOW_UPDATE_START/END protected region convention for epoch-boundary durable guidance (analogous to dream cycle for memory layer), train/selection 70/30 split of eval records.

files.description: New skill: trajectory-to-edits reflection engine. Core component of skill-optimize workflow. Loads eval records and session transcripts, partitions into success/failure minibatches, analyzes failure patterns, proposes corrective edits, filters against rejected-edit buffer, applies edit budget, writes structured JSON to candidates/round-{N}-edits.json. Edit schema: {op, target, content, pattern_type, affected_runs, source, priority_rank}. Respects all protected regions (system:start/end, personal:start/end, SLOW_UPDATE_START/END).

8-step orchestrating workflow for SkillOpt-style skill optimization. Termination conditions: rounds exhausted, 3 consecutive zero-edit rounds, size ceiling (max_token_budget), controller termination. STATE CHECK protocol on entry. Owned by Rigby.

Initial state template for skill-optimize workflow. Fields: skill_id, skill_path, edit_budget (default 4), total_rounds (default 4), epoch_size (default 2), rounds_completed, consecutive_zero_edit_rounds, baseline_score, best_score, best_skill_path, eval_record_ids[], selection_record_ids[], rejected_edits_path, slow_update_history_path, accepted_edits_total, last_round_delta, max_token_budget (default 2000).

Step 1: Configure target skill, scan eval records from both systems/eval-harness/runs/ and systems/evals/ directories, apply 70/30 train/selection split, create candidates/ directory, initialize rejected-edits.json buffer.
Step 2: Score all selection records using score_eval.py, handle no-assertions case (neutral 0.5 with warning surfaced to controller), initialize best_score = baseline_score in state.yaml.
Step 3: Invoke rigby-skill-reflect with train batch. Handle insufficient_data flag (skip to step-08 with note). Handle zero edits (increment consecutive_zero_edit_rounds counter, proceed to gate).

Step 4: Load best_skill_path, apply edits in priority order, respect all protected regions (system:start/end, personal:start/end, SLOW_UPDATE_START/END). Write to candidates/round-{N}-candidate.md only — never overwrites SKILL.md directly. Adds traceability header comment.

Step 5: Score candidate against selection records using score_eval.py. IES adaptation: simulated_improvement assessment checks if accepted edits directly address specific failed assertions. Compute delta = candidate_score - best_score.

Step 6: Strict delta > 0 gate (ties rejected). Accept: copy candidate to SKILL.md, update best_score, log to pending-changes. Reject: SKILL.md unchanged. Always update rejected-edits buffer. Determine next step dynamically (slow update at epoch boundary, report at termination, reflect otherwise).

Step 7: Epoch-boundary consolidation. Reads all round outputs for the epoch, synthesizes longitudinal guidance (what worked/didn't/is durable), writes to SLOW_UPDATE_START/END protected region (max 300 tokens). Gates through same validation before committing. Updates slow-update-history.json.

Step 8: Final report. Computes statistics (rounds, accepted/rejected, delta), generates skill diff, writes optimization-report-{YYYY-MM-DD}.md, cleans candidate directory (keep winner + latest edit JSON), confirms pending-changes current, sets state.yaml status: complete.

Authoritative Python implementation of IES composite scoring formula. CLI: --record, --batch, --skill, --limit, --pretty, --summary. Functions: find_record() (checks runs/ then evals/**/ recursively), find_records_for_skill() (scans both directories, sorts by started desc), compute_score() (implements formula with null weight redistribution, returns score/components/notes), score_batch() (per-record + aggregate stats).
